subject: Information Theory
title: Spread Spectrum
description: Learn Spread Spectrum in one minute.

hook.text: GPS satellites transmit below the noise floor. The signal is weaker than static—yet your phone finds it perfectly.

buildup.text: Spread spectrum spreads a signal across a wide frequency band using a pseudorandom code known to the receiver.

discovery.text: The receiver correlates with the code, concentrating the signal back while noise stays spread. SNR jumps dramatically.

twist.text: Hedy Lamarr co-invented frequency hopping in 1942 for torpedo guidance. It became the basis of modern spread spectrum.

climax.text: CDMA, GPS, Bluetooth, and military radios all use spread spectrum for resilience, security, and interference rejection.

punchline.text: Hide in the noise. Only the right code finds you.

quiz.question: How does a spread spectrum receiver extract the signal?
options: By correlating with a known pseudorandom code
